A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, and central results. All 38 pages of each version, including equations, figures, algorithms, and appendices, support comparison despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical guarantees and proofs, including in its appendices. Figures 1–2 illustrate comparator interpolation and constructed functions; they do not report experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical. Its added strongly convex analysis supplies an algorithm and proof, while neither the main text nor the appendices report empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds a strongly convex K-ONS/mirror-descent instantiation using feature-covariance weighting, alongside the retained exp-concave algorithm using gradient-feature products. The central reduction, Algorithms 1–2, and spectral kernel remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation tasks. The strongly convex addition is a theoretical setting, not an evaluated test scenario.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. References to other algorithms concern mathematical guarantees rather than reported baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies experimental splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures. The new algorithmic parameters belong to the theoretical development.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness experiments, or empirical error analyses. Figure 2 retains the same illustrative function construction with m = 1 and T = 5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated empirical runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries, rankings, or measured findings are added or changed. The illustrative curves are retained; additions and corrections to mathematical bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 adds a substantive proof branch for strongly convex losses: Proposition 9, Theorem 7 and its proof in Appendix F.1, supported by the new norm identity in Lemma 8. It also corrects existing mathematics, including G to G0 in Proposition 6 and the integral bound from 2L to L in the spectral-density proof. The central path-length theorems remain intact.

C1.justification: v2 makes the unbounded-domain focus and comparator-magnitude dependence explicit, and includes strongly convex losses in the introductory contribution statement. v1 already mentioned strong convexity in Section 3, so this is a limited clarification and elevation of scope; the central novelty claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 and new Appendix D explain the spectral-density choice and regularization, while Section 5 explains effective dimension and the significance of squared path-length guarantees. Appendix F.1 adds a lower-bound argument against eliminating comparator-norm dependence. Existing computational limitations and the unresolved TV-optimal kernel construction remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3, footnote 5, newly explains enforcing bounded outputs through an unconstrained-to-constrained reduction in the original decision space. v1 Appendix D.5 instead specified an operator-level constraint set. No code, hardware, or empirical implementation information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Jacobsen and Cutkosky (2024) on regression via discounting and Zhang, Zhao, and Sugiyama (2025) on curved losses. It replaces Yueh (2005) with three tridiagonal-matrix references. The main positioning relative to earlier dynamic-to-static reductions is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds explanatory passages, loss-type subheadings, and funding acknowledgments, and reorganizes the appendices, including moving scale-free guarantees from D.5 to C.3. Citation style and notation are revised, but the main section sequence and most existing prose remain.

P2.justification: A document-wide switch to NeurIPS formatting changes typography, margins, title-page styling, algorithm formatting, and bibliography layout. Figures 1–2 retain their content but are resized and reflowed with the text. This is extensive visual reformatting without new experimental displays.

improvement.justification: The explicit strongly convex algorithm and proof in F.1, together with corrections in Proposition 6 and the spectral-density proof, improve completeness and precision. The central reduction and main guarantees remain unchanged. Added exposition has a local flaw: Appendix D states a |omega|^-2 tail bound although its taper implies |omega|^-3/2 decay. Integrability still follows, so this does not outweigh the limited gains.
